_areas_note: SPLIT from Mount Olympus. The research also corrected my prompt's conflation of 'Constance Pass' with 'Lake Constance' — they are separate basins on opposite sides of the massif, and Home Lake below Constance Pass does NOT serve the standard South Chute. That site is kept but says so in its own notes.

sites.name: Lake Constance — the standard base for the South Chute
sites.capacity: HARD overnight quota of 20 people for the whole basin; roughly five individual sites plus one group site are commonly reported, and parties of seven or more must take the group site
sites.water: Reliable at the lake itself. Constance Creek, which the climbers' trail follows, runs well early in the season and can be dry by late summer — carry water up rather than assuming you will find it on the climb.
sites.permit: Olympic Wilderness Permit required and Lake Constance is a NAMED QUOTA AREA. Reserve on Recreation.gov; the 20-person cap makes this one of the scarcest permits in the Olympics. Bear canisters required. Older write-ups describing a free self-issued permit at the trailhead are OUT OF DATE.
sites.notes: The base camp for essentially every ascent by the standard South Chute, reached by a savage climbers' path that gains roughly 3,300 to 3,400 ft in under two miles of hand-over-hand scrambling above the Dosewallips road. Published elevations for the lake vary between about 4,650 and 4,800 ft, a fair reflection of how imprecise everything about this approach is. From camp the route runs north into Avalanche Canyon and then up the chute toward the south ridge notch, so a summit day from here is short by Olympic standards. The 20-person ceiling is the real planning constraint — it is a basin, not a campground, and it is full most fine weekends.

sites.name: Dosewallips road-end camps, staging for the washed-out road
sites.capacity: Several riverside sites in and around the old drive-in campground at the end of the closed road, plus sites near Dose Forks; rarely full
sites.permit: Olympic Wilderness Permit required for any night inside the park boundary, booked on Recreation.gov. Bear canisters required. Sites on the Forest Service side of the boundary below the park have their own rules, so check which side of the line you intend to sleep on.
sites.notes: THE ROAD HAS BEEN CLOSED BY A WASHOUT SINCE THE EARLY 2000s, so what used to be a drive-in trailhead is now several miles of road walking — the park's own figure adds about 6.5 miles to the round trip, and other accounts quote over five miles each way to the Lake Constance turn-off, so plan on the longer number. Parties who cannot face the road walk and the 3,400 ft climbers' trail in one day use the old campground area as a staging night, then hit the path fresh in the morning. It is the single biggest variable on this side of the range and it rules out a casual car-to-car attempt for most people. Bikes are allowed on the closed road and cut the approach time significantly.

sites.name: Home Lake, below Constance Pass — NOT the standard Constance camp
sites.capacity: A few small individual sites in an exposed subalpine basin
sites.water: Reliable — the lake, and it is the last dependable water before the pass
sites.permit: Olympic Wilderness Permit required, reserved on Recreation.gov. Bear canisters required, and no fires are permitted at this elevation.
sites.notes: Home Lake sits just below Constance Pass and is a genuine high camp, but it MUST NOT BE CONFUSED WITH LAKE CONSTANCE — it does not serve the South Chute and cannot substitute for the quota at the lake. Parties camp here for the Inner Constance country, the northern approaches and traverses, or as a through-hike stop, and reaching it from the Dosewallips means the full road walk plus a long valley trail rather than the short brutal climbers' path. If your objective is the standard route, this is the wrong basin. Its practical value to a Constance trip is as a bail-out when the 20-person quota at the lake is gone.
